text: The purpose of this analysis was to examine participants’ social interaction anxiety, attachment anxiety, and self-esteem using psychological survey data. The data were cleaned and scored in R. Descriptive statistics and internal consistency estimates were calculated for each psychological scale, and an additional analysis was conducted for male participants.

Measures
Social Interaction Anxiety. Social interaction anxiety was measured using the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale. Items 5, 9, and 11 were reverse-keyed prior to calculating participants’ average scale scores. The scale demonstrated an internal consistency of α = 0.9.
Attachment Anxiety. Attachment anxiety was measured using the Experiences in Close Relationships Anxiety Subscale. Participants’ responses were averaged to produce an attachment anxiety score. The scale demonstrated an internal consistency of α = 0.94.
Self-Esteem. Self-esteem was measured using the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale. Items 2, 5, 6, 8, and 9 were reverse-keyed prior to calculating participants’ average scale scores. The scale demonstrated an internal consistency of α = 0.85.


Data Analysis Strategy
Survey responses were cleaned and demographic variables were assigned informative labels prior to analysis. Scale scores were calculated separately for social interaction anxiety, attachment anxiety, and self-esteem using scoreItems(). Reverse-keyed items were specified when scoring the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale and Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale. Average scores and Cronbach’s alpha values were then calculated for each scale. Descriptive statistics were calculated for the full sample and subsequently for a filtered dataset containing only male participants.
